title: Finite coefficient change for closed support
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, let $m,n\geq1$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism between the finite coefficient rings $A=A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ and $B=A_{L,n}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$ of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. This includes coefficient reduction and finite coefficient-field extension at compatible levels; flatness of $B$ over $A$ is not assumed. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ and a complex $K$ of $A$-module sheaves on $T$ put $K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$, the derived change of rings on constant coefficient sheaves [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $X,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Work on the small pro-etale sites, with the finite constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the derived direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Then the canonical comparison
$$
b_{i,M}:(Ri_A^!M)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_B^!(M_B)
$$
is an isomorphism. It is the adjoint, under $i_{*,B}\dashv Ri_B^!$, of
$$
i_{*,B}((Ri_A^!M)_B)\xrightarrow{\ c_{i,Ri_A^!M}^{-1}\ }(i_{*,A}Ri_A^!M)_B\xrightarrow{\ (\varepsilon_{i,A,M})_B\ }M_B,
$$
where $c_{i,N}:(i_{*,A}N)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{*,B}(N_B)$ is the canonical ordinary direct-image coefficient comparison and $\varepsilon_{i,A,M}$ is the exceptional counit. Both sides lie in $D^b_{ctf}(Z,B)$. The comparison is natural in $M$, commutes with the exceptional counit, and is compatible with composition of closed immersions and successive homomorphisms between finite coefficient stages, under the canonical composition and iterated derived change-of-rings identifications.

For a locally closed immersion $h:W\hookrightarrow X$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, choose an open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ and a factorization $W\xrightarrow{k}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ in which $k$ is closed and $j$ is open. The corresponding assertion holds for $Rh^!=Rk^!j^*$: the comparison is the closed comparison applied to $j^*M$, composed with the coefficient comparison for open restriction. It is natural in $M$, has the same exceptional-counit compatibility, respects successive coefficient changes, and respects composition of closed immersions inside the chosen open $V$.

proof.text: Put $N=Ri_A^!M$. [lem-coef-closed-scalar-domains] gives bounded constructible etale origins and the required Tor intervals for $M_B$, $N$, $N_B$ and $Ri_B^!M_B$, without assuming $B/A$ flat. Its assertion applies at each intermediate finite coefficient stage.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; assembly of extracted work items, step 1

proof.text: For the complementary open $j$, [lem-coef-localization-scalar-unit] supplies the two distinguished triangles, the ordinary isomorphism $c_i$, and the third-vertex isomorphism $d_j$ satisfying the open-unit square. Apply [lem-coef-localization-first-transpose] with $\mathcal T_R=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ and $\mathcal C_R=D^b_{ctf}(Z,R)$ for $R=A,B$, which are triangulated subcategories stable under $i_{*,R}$, $Ri_R^!$ and $(-)_B$ by clauses (2'), (3') of [prop-sf-localization-all-stages] and step 1, so that the adjunction restricts and both triangles lie in them; take $I_R=i_{*,R}$, $J_R=Ri_R^!$, $S_X=(-)_B$, $S_Z=(-)_B$ and $c=c_i$. Its full-faithfulness hypothesis is [prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages]. It gives an invertible first component $a$ with $a c_i^{-1}=i_{*,B}(b_{i,M})$, for precisely the counit-defined map in the statement. Thus $i_{*,B}(b_{i,M})$ is invertible. Full faithfulness reflects isomorphisms: lift its inverse and use faithfulness to check both inverse identities. Hence $b_{i,M}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; assembly of extracted work items, step 2

proof.text: [lem-coef-closed-transpose-cocycles] applies to these ordinary comparisons on the domains of step 1. Its defining equation gives the exceptional-counit compatibility and naturality; its two cocycles give composition of closed immersions and successive finite coefficient maps under the stated chained adjunctions and balancing associators. The Lean naturality clause is now proved directly: convert the supplied finite-Tor domains to bounded etale origins using the finite-ring origin equivalence; use the relative exceptional Hom bijection to make composition with the B-counit injective. Naturality of the inverse ordinary coefficient comparison and of the A- and B-exceptional counits makes the two transposes equal. The composition and coefficient cocycles remain proof obligations.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; assembly of extracted work items, step 3

proof.text: For the chosen factorization $h=jt$ with $t$ closed and $j$ open, [lem-coef-open-scalar-adjunction-counit] identifies $Rh_!=j_!t_*$, $Rh^!=Rt^!j^*$ and the composite counit, checks their domains, and supplies the $B$-linear open coefficient isomorphism $e_j$ and its counit equation. Put $b_h=Rt_B^!(r_j)b_{t,j_A^*M}$ with its canonical open restriction isomorphism $r_j$. The closed result applied to $j_A^*M$ makes both factors invertible; the same domain assertion and step 1 put both endpoints in $D^b_{ctf}(W,B)$.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; assembly of extracted work items, step 4

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-locally-closed-scalar-pasting] to the closed families of step 3 and the open maps of step 4. Its explicit counit identity proves the required locally closed exceptional-counit compatibility. Its naturality and its two pasted identities give successive coefficient compatibility and composition of closed immersions inside the chosen open $V$. The restriction comparison satisfies the required tensor-associativity compatibility by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The Lean locally closed naturality clause is proved directly from the closed naturality clause: exact pullback preserves the finite-Tor predicate, translating bounded constructibility by the finite-ring origin equivalence and the Tor interval by lem-exc-intrinsic-tor-amplitude-transport. Paste closed naturality at j^*f with naturality of the inverse canonical scalar/pullback isomorphism. The remaining pasted counit and cocycle clauses remain proof obligations.

lean.statement: theorem finiteCoefficientClosedShriek (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (E L : Type u) [Field E] [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] [Algebra (Padic l) L] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L] (m n : ℕ) (φ : ULift.{u + 1, u} (finiteClosedCoefficient l E m) →+* ULift.{u + 1, u} (finiteClosedCoefficient l L n)) (X Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))) [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated Z.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom] [QuasiCompact Z.hom] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i.left] (M : finiteClosedDerived X.left (finiteClosedCoefficient l E m)) (_hM : finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l E (m + 1) (Nat.succ_pos m) X.left M) : (∃! b, IsFiniteClosedShriekMap φ i.left M b) ∧ IsFiniteClosedShriekMap φ i.left M (finiteClosedShriekMap φ i.left M) ∧ IsIso (ProEtale.finiteCoefficientChangeDirectImageMap φ i.left ((finiteClosedExceptional (finiteClosedCoefficient l E m) i.left).obj M)) ∧ IsIso (finiteClosedShriekMap φ i.left M) ∧ finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l L (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) X.left ((finiteClosedScalar φ X.left).obj M) ∧ finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l L (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z.left ((finiteClosedScalar φ Z.left).obj ((finiteClosedExceptional (finiteClosedCoefficient l E m) i.left).obj M)) ∧ finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l L (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z.left ((finiteClosedExceptional (finiteClosedCoefficient l L n) i.left).obj ((finiteClosedScalar φ X.left).obj M))
